children: Merrill will offer its financial advisors new incentives next year to provide clients with banking and lending services from parent company Bank of America. The changes, which are part of the company's 2027 advisor compensation plan, are part of a yearslong push by Merrill to get its advisors to sell more banking services.

Merrill informed its advisors of the changes, which include a new bonus and a tweak to an existing award, on Thursday. The brokerage firm left its so-called pay grid unchanged, however. A central feature of compensation plans at national brokerage firms, the grid determines advisors' core compensation based on how much annual revenue they generate.

"We look at compensation every year to make sure it supports our long-term strategy and rewards advisors for strong performance," Patricio Diaz, chief operating officer at Merrill, said in a statement. "This year, that meant making a few targeted updates that reflect the evolving needs of our clients and the breadth of capabilities our advisors bring to them."

Merrill has been trying to grow the services it offers clients beyond investments. Under the company's 2027 plan, advisors will be able to earn a new cash bonus that rewards them for increasing the loans they make to clients. Advisors can earn 10 basis points, or 0.1%, on annual net new lending flows of at least $10 million and 20 basis points, or 0.2%, on annual net new lending flows that are at least $25 million.

Merrill is also amending an existing growth award that it introduced in 2024 by increasing qualification requirements as well as providing more ways to win bonuses. As part of the revised qualification requirements, advisors must have full-year net strategic flows of at least $7.5 million, up from $5 million, and they must also earn at least four credits for bringing in new client households, up from three credits. (The number of credits an advisor earns depends on the size of the household.) Advisors who qualify for the growth award can win a 50% premium on their standard growth award by recording at least $50 million in net new annual managed flows, or at least $10 million in net new annual bank checking and savings flows, or $10 million in net new annual lending flows. Advisors can qualify in one or more categories, which replace a current requirement of achieving more than $150 million in strategic flows.

Merrill executives believe the core features of its compensation plan, introduced in 2023, have been delivering results, with the vast majority of advisors improving their growth rates, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Merrill is one of the nation's largest wealth management companies and had $4.2 trillion in client balances as of the end of the third quarter, up 9% from a year ago. Merrill is part of Bank of America's Global Wealth and Investment Management division, which also includes a private bank. During the third quarter, the unit added about 5,000 net new accounts belonging to households with $500,000 or more in invested assets. The division posted record revenue of $7.1 billion for the third quarter, up 13% year over year.

Merrill competitors UBS and Morgan Stanley have unveiled their annual advisor compensation plans. Like Merrill, UBS added new incentives for advisors to grow banking and lending services with their clients. Morgan Stanley raised grid thresholds, meaning advisors may have to generate more revenue to earn the same payout next year. Wells Fargo, the fourth so-called wirehouse, has yet to reveal its 2027 plan.
